I was with the reviewer all the way to the end. Then this happened:

A Linux system will almost always have better hardware support,

Ok, this guy likes Linux on his embedded devices. That's fine. He can't possibly be saying that all devices are better supported on Linux.

and this is especially true on embedded devices.

Oh....

You can put Linux on over 20 different architectures. Can you say the same for Windows? The performance (drivers and all) may be shotty when compared to Windows, but the hardware support is better on Linux then Windows.

If you're wondering:

Windows: ARM, IA-32, Itanium, x86-64

Linux: Alpha, ARC, ARM, AVR32, Blackfin, C6x, ETRAX CRIS, FR-V, H8/300, Hexagon, Itanium, M32R, m68k, META, Microblaze, MIPS, MN103, Nios II, OpenRISC, PA-RISC, PowerPC, s390, S+core, SuperH, SPARC, TILE64, Unicore32, x86, Xtensa

I feel like this reviewer tried to review a product for what it was never intended to be. This is the first release of an OS developed for an IoT that hasn't been developed yet, this isn't so you can have Windows 10 on literally every microcontroller ever developed.
